title: Open the terminal only when no custom instruction is supplied

intentCoverage.report:
# Dough Intent Coverage — SEED-320#open-terminal-only-without-a-custom-instruction

**Verdict: Caught.** The maintained assertion `await expect(followUp(entry, retiredTitle)).toBeFocused({ timeout: launchWaitMs })` (`dashboard/tests/launches/agent-launch-follow-up-session.spec.ts:112`, test "a Done session whose workspace is gone offers Read final report and Follow up; Start sends the context with the request, opens nothing, returns the keyboard to Follow up and leaves the source as it was") failed on independently observed wrong behavior. The claim is limited to this path: an instructed Follow up from a Recently done entry whose workspace is gone, Claude Code host, Side panel closed.

**Next proof action:** none needed for this promise on this path; the maintained assertion holds it.

## What was checked

- **Story and revision:** `.planning/seeds/SEED-320-conditional-terminal-opening.md`, "Open the terminal only when no custom instruction is supplied"; plan `.planning/slice-plans/597-open-terminal-only-without-a-custom-instruction/PLAN.md`; revision `14664612e2d627de4767c034de205e1688db175f`.
- **Promise:** key example "Side panel closed, instruction typed in **Follow up** → Start → the Side panel stays closed and the keyboard returns to **Follow up**" (scope: "The keyboard returns to the button that started it when it still rests on the startup's progress").
- **Fault (one edit):** `dashboard/src/launchDialogLauncher.ts` — the keyboard-return effect changed from `useLayoutEffect` to `useEffect` (import and call; 2 lines). The caller's hints were validated and reused unchanged: the plan's slice 2 learning records exactly this ordering dependency against `dashboard/src/recentlyDoneFocus.ts`, and the hinted test and command exist at the revision.
- **Fixture:** the spec's own (`reported` launch record, `claudeScenario("launched")`); fixtures and assertions were left intact.
- **Command (scratch checkout root, 1 worker):** `caffeinate -s -i env -u NO_COLOR -u FORCE_COLOR -u GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES npm run test:dashboard -- --reporter=list --workers=1 dashboard/tests/launches/agent-launch-follow-up-session.spec.ts`

## Run observations

1. **Setup:** isolated detached worktree at the revision under `/Users/terryyin/.claude/jobs/70d8eb8f/tmp/ic-scratch`; `setup-native.mjs npm` and `check` passed first time (Node 24.21.0, Chromium 158.0.8127.18); pre-probe `git status` clean.
2. **Baseline:** 2 passed (9.6 s; target test 3.1 s). Load average about 13.
3. **Faulted:** 2 failed. The target test failed at line 112, `toBeFocused`: "Expected: focused / Received: inactive", with the locator resolved to the Follow up button 58 times. The run ended on "Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded" only because the assertion's own wait (`launchWaitMs` = 30 000 ms) equals the test timeout; this is the assertion failing, not fixture time — every earlier step, including the new Taken entry appearing and the dialog hiding, had passed, and the baseline test took 3.1 s. Load average 10–15.
   The spec's second test (whitespace-only Follow up) also failed, at line 189 (`.xterm-helper-textarea` `toBeFocused`): the same fault leaves the keyboard out of the presented terminal, consistent with the plan's learning. That is a second maintained catch of the same fault on a different promise; it was not independently witnessed here.
4. **Reach and wrong behavior, observed independently:** a temporary scratch spec (copy of the target test up to the dialog hiding, then waiting for Follow up to be enabled and reading `document.activeElement` on five animation frames, with no focus assertion) reported, under the fault, the keyboard on `ARTICLE` "Ad hoc session for Why is the CI slow on main?" — the source entry — on all five readings, with the Side panel count 0. The same witness after restoration reported `BUTTON` "Follow up Why is the CI slow on main?" on the readings kept (the first three; the printed line was cut before the last two). So the fault sends the keyboard to the source entry instead of Follow up, on the path the maintained test exercises; the Side panel half of the promise was unaffected by this fault and is not covered by this verdict.
5. **Restoration:** `git checkout` of the one file, byte-identical to the pre-probe copy (`cmp`); witness spec and test results deleted; `git status` clean at `14664612e`; the same command then gave 2 passed (11.5 s; target test 5.4 s; load average rising to 28). The scratch worktree was removed with `git worktree remove`; the story worktree was never edited and the shared stash never touched.

## Prior disposition

The evidence matches the plan's recorded slice 2 learning (the launcher places the keyboard in a layout effect because Recently done's held-entry rescue otherwise takes it first) and the proof-ownership row "Keyboard returns to the launching button — closed-panel journey, Start session and Follow up". This is recognition of existing proof; the probe causes no new repair decision.

## Cost

- **Test runtime.** About 117 s of Playwright runner time in total: baseline 9.6 s, witness under fault 15.4 s, witness restored 14.5 s, restored 11.5 s (each measured, runner-reported totals); faulted run about 66 s (estimated: two tests at 30.3 s and 30.2 s measured, plus build and setup overhead the runner did not total).
- **Human effort.** Unavailable: no human took part in the probe and no measure of the requester's time was observed.
- **Agent effort.** 8 tool steps by one agent (measured, counted from this run: one lookup, one setup, four test-running or inspection steps, one cleanup, one report); token use unavailable — not exposed to the agent.


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 190830 ms (measured), from 1794456001677 to 1794456192507 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.
  The start clock was sampled one tool step after work began (after reading the skill, story and plan), so this interval omits that first lookup.

---

## Wrap-up disposition

- Checked revision: `14664612e2d627de4767c034de205e1688db175f`.
- Evidence: the report above (Caught; the maintained Follow up keyboard assertion failed on the independently observed wrong behavior, and the restored run passed).
- Decision: no follow-up. The probe protects only this promise on this path; it shows no delivered defect and no proof gap.
- Canonical follow-up links: none.
